paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.

model_annotations.English: The plot titled “Errors (BoolQ)” illustrates how an error metric varies with adapter rank for the BoolQ setting, showing a single series with vertical error bars. The x-axis is labeled “Rank” and displays discrete tick values at 4, 16, 64, and 256 (spaced evenly while increasing multiplicatively), spanning from 4 to 256 with no units indicated. The y-axis has no explicit label but is scaled linearly from 0.0 to 0.6, with major ticks at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, and 0.6. A single black solid line connects large green circular markers at each rank: the value is approximately 0.27 at rank 4, decreases to about 0.24 at rank 16, increases to about 0.30 at rank 64, and rises further to about 0.35 at rank 256. Each point includes a vertical black error bar with caps; for example, the rank-4 point spans roughly from about 0.19 to 0.35, rank 16 from about 0.15 to 0.34, rank 64 from about 0.21 to 0.39, and rank 256 from about 0.27 to 0.42.
model_annotations.German: The plot titled “Errors (BoolQ)” illustrates how an error metric varies with adapter rank, showing a single series with uncertainty bars across four rank settings. The x-axis is labeled “Rank” and displays discrete tick labels at 4, 16, 64, and 256 (no units shown), with the points laid out at evenly spaced positions corresponding to these values. The y-axis has unlabeled units and spans from 0.0 to 0.6 on a linear scale, with regularly spaced tick marks every 0.2 (0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6). One black solid line connects large green circular markers at each rank, and each marker has a vertical black error bar with horizontal caps. The series starts at rank 4 near 0.27 (error bar extending roughly from about 0.19 to 0.36), dips at rank 16 to about 0.24–0.25 (roughly ~0.15 to ~0.34), rises at rank 64 to around 0.30 (roughly ~0.22 to ~0.39), and increases again at rank 256 to about 0.35 (roughly ~0.27 to ~0.42).
